beats.headline: The best source on the ninth
beats.text: For the record: the subject enters the file as a thought. Crawler Carl sits in the saferoom while the children watch The Last Unicorn, with tens of thousands of NPC deaths planned for phase four, and thinks of two Cookbook authors. One is Coolie. The other is Priestly, who wrote the fourteenth edition and is the single best source of information on the ninth floor. He wonders what either would do in his position. Coolie would do exactly what he is doing. Priestly would not.

beats.headline: A living, breathing poem
beats.text: Fourteenth edition. Larracos is like a dream, the subject writes, a living, breathing poem. An inverted funnel of museums, galleries, colleges and colour, layered like a cone going deeper. The NPCs live there, with purpose and life, and for the first time since he was dragged into this he feels awe instead of rage. It is too beautiful to be used this way, and too real not to be a copy of somewhere that existed. Tonight, before the crawlers are expelled, he plans to sit down and watch a play.

beats.headline: He fears for his mind
beats.text: The same note turns. The aliens who buy their weapons in the pleasure districts are expelled with the crawlers, less than thirty hours before the fighting begins, and return once only three armies remain. By the time it is over, they say, none of the NPCs are left alive and none of the buildings stand, all for an imaginary prize. It makes his heart hurt. He offers to draw a map; the one Milk drew is still good but lacks detail. He fears what happens to his mind when he sees the city destroyed.

beats.headline: So much. So little.
beats.text: The crawler counter falls under a hundred thousand, and Crawler Carl thinks of the subject. The system broke him. Seeing that city destroyed as he marched with the bugbear army over the bodies of the NPCs, among them actors he had watched in a play, finally snapped what sanity he had left. His last entry came shortly after, an incoherent jumble. So much. So little. Stab, stab, stab. If I fall, if I stand. It matters not when the song is done.

beats.headline: The trap he fell into
beats.text: Crawler Carl has just killed a great many innocent NPCs, and weighs it against the subject. Priestly fell into the trap of caring so much it paralysed him into inaction, and it broke him. Crawler Carl decides he is not going to make the same mistake: this is war, and the NPCs he killed were spared a bloody conflict that ended in their deaths anyway. A distant part of him is alarmed at this attitude. The file records both parts.

beats.headline: Stab, stab, stab
beats.text: Fourteenth edition, second-to-last entry. It is the final days of Faction Wars, the orcs are going to win, and the army the subject was conscripted into is going to fall; he writes that he dies tomorrow. The bugbears march in the morning and laugh at everything. Conscripts in his squad plan to flee into the forest. His people number three hundred, down from millions, and the real gods have not intervened. He hopes there is music. Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, adds: do not read the last one. He does not make it to the battle once he sees what happened to Larracos.

beats.headline: What the Conscript spell hid
beats.text: Crawler Carl leads a party into a tower lobby while the sluggalos who came with him run back into the city. During the real Faction Wars, he could open his warlord menu and force them back into line. That, the file notes, is something Priestly and several other Cookbook authors before him did not know about the Conscript spell.

beats.headline: The city he meant
beats.text: Entering the Larracos College of Magic. Crawler Carl steps outside and, for the first time, sees the city whole: towers growing out of the ring like crystals, an alabaster saferoom tower wrapped in flowering vines, an observatory, the scent of drained ocean under the flowers. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who loved this city so much it drove him mad to see it destroyed. Now he can see what Priestly meant. It is like something out of a Tolkien novel.

beats.headline: His greatest desires
beats.text: Fourteenth edition. In the absolute, scorching heat of battle, the subject writes, one learns who one really is and what one really wants. One faces one's greatest fears and, much worse, one's greatest desires laid bare. For him they are the same, and it is his devastation. Stab, stab, stab. The note sits in the Cookbook while Crawler Carl's people hold the entrance of a castle under pulse rifle fire.

beats.headline: Slam, slam, slam
beats.text: At the bottom of Larracos, Crawler Carl walks through ruin: walls scarred as if by electrical strikes, the roof long gone, wet slime and ash, a smell of burned fish, rotten milk and sulfur. Red ash rains on everything. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who went insane at the sight of this city after it had fallen. Stab, stab, stab, he thinks. Slam, slam, slam. A statue that once stood at the entrance lies shattered, glittering in the ash.
